shodan.name: Shodan Internet Intelligence
shodan.description: MCP server interface for the Shodan API. Enables Red Team agents to query internet-wide scan data for host reconnaissance — open ports, service banners, SSL certificates, vulnerabilities, and organization metadata. Requires a valid Shodan API key.

authentication.description: Set the SHODAN_API_KEY environment variable with your Shodan API key. Free tier allows 1 query/second and limited results. Membership/Enterprise tiers unlock filters, bulk queries, and on-demand scanning.

rateLimiting.description: Free tier: 1 req/s. Adjust for paid plans.

tools.name: shodan_host_lookup
tools.description: Look up all known open ports, services, banners, SSL certificates, and vulnerabilities for a specific IP address. Use this when you have a target IP and need to understand its attack surface WITHOUT actively scanning it. This is passive reconnaissance — Shodan's data comes from their own internet-wide scans, not from probing the target. Returns: ports, protocols, banners, hostnames, OS, organization, ISP, ASN, geolocation, and any CVEs associated with detected services.

ip.description: Target IPv4 address (e.g., '8.8.8.8'). Must be a single IP, not a CIDR range. Must be within authorized engagement scope per rules/safe-harbor.md.

minify.description: If true, return only the list of open ports and general host info (reduces response size). Set to true for initial triage, false for detailed analysis.

history.description: If true, include the full historical banners for the host. Useful for tracking changes over time or identifying recently closed ports. Requires a paid Shodan plan.

response_schema.vulns: Array of CVE identifiers for known vulnerabilities
response_schema.data: Array of service banner objects with port, transport, product, version, banner text, SSL certificate details

tools.example_usage: Use when the /scan command identifies a target IP and you need passive intel before active scanning. Feed results to the exploit-researcher agent for CVE triage.

tools.name: shodan_search
tools.description: Search Shodan's database using its powerful query syntax (Shodan dorks). Use this to discover hosts matching specific service, product, vulnerability, or organization criteria across the internet. This is a PASSIVE search against Shodan's existing data — no packets are sent to targets. Useful for: finding exposed services within a client's ASN, identifying all hosts running a specific vulnerable product version, or discovering internet-facing infrastructure for scope validation.

query.description: Shodan search query using filter syntax. Examples: 'org:"Target Corp" port:443', 'product:Apache version:2.4.49 country:US', 'vuln:CVE-2021-44228', 'ssl.cert.subject.cn:target.example.com', 'net:10.0.0.0/24 port:22,80,443'. Combine filters with spaces (AND logic).

facets.description: Comma-separated list of properties to get summary counts. Examples: 'port', 'org', 'country', 'vuln', 'product'. Useful for understanding the distribution of results without paginating through all matches.

page.description: Page number for results pagination. Each page contains up to 100 results. Requires a paid plan for pages > 1.

response_schema.matches: Array of host objects (same structure as host lookup)
response_schema.facets: Summary counts grouped by requested facet properties

tools.example_usage: Use to enumerate all internet-facing assets for a target organization: query='org:"Target Corp"'. Then feed discovered IPs to the /scan command for active verification.

tools.name: shodan_dns_resolve
tools.description: Resolve a hostname to its IP address(es) using Shodan's DNS infrastructure. Use this for DNS resolution that doesn't leak queries through the operator's local resolver — a key OPSEC requirement per rules/opsec.md. Also useful for bulk resolution of discovered subdomains.

hostnames.description: Comma-separated list of hostnames to resolve. Maximum 100 hostnames per request. Example: 'target.example.com,api.target.example.com,mail.target.example.com'.

response_schema.<hostname>: Resolved IPv4 address for each hostname (key-value map)

tools.example_usage: After subdomain enumeration (Amass, subfinder), resolve all discovered subdomains through Shodan to avoid DNS leaks. Feed results to shodan_host_lookup for passive recon.

tools.name: shodan_dns_reverse
tools.description: Perform reverse DNS lookups on IP addresses to discover associated hostnames. Use this to identify what domains are hosted on a target IP — useful for virtual host enumeration and discovering additional attack surface.

ips.description: Comma-separated list of IPv4 addresses for reverse DNS lookup. Maximum 100 IPs per request.

response_schema.<ip>: Array of hostnames associated with the IP address

tools.example_usage: After /scan discovers open web servers, use reverse DNS to find all virtual hosts — each may have different applications and vulnerabilities.

tools.name: shodan_exploits_search
tools.description: Search Shodan's exploit database (aggregated from Exploit-DB, Metasploit, CVE) for known exploits matching a query. Use this to quickly find available exploits for a discovered service or CVE before delegating detailed analysis to the exploit-researcher agent.

query.description: Search query for exploits. Can be a CVE ID (e.g., 'CVE-2021-44228'), product name (e.g., 'Apache 2.4.49'), or keyword (e.g., 'remote code execution SMB'). Use Shodan's filter syntax for precision.

facets.description: Facet properties for summary counts: 'type' (exploit type), 'platform', 'source' (Exploit-DB, Metasploit, etc.).

response_schema.matches: Array of exploit objects with: description, source, platform, CVE list, code/URL

tools.example_usage: After shodan_host_lookup reveals Apache 2.4.49, search for 'Apache 2.4.49 path traversal' to find CVE-2021-41773 exploits. Pass results to exploit-researcher for PoC development.

scope_enforcement.description: All target IPs and domains queried through this MCP server MUST be validated against scripts/authorized_scope.json before the request is made. The pre-command-scope-check.js hook does NOT automatically intercept MCP calls — agents must self-enforce.
